examples.title: Relative risk with a sentence
examples.prompt: 1000 expectant mothers reported whether they took folate supplements, and their infants were checked for neural tube defects (NTDs). A \(\chi^2\) test found a difference (\(P<0.01\)). Quantify the association between the mother not taking folate and NTDs in one sentence a newspaper reader could follow.

steps.say: The mothers were enrolled during pregnancy and the infants were checked afterwards. So the study is prospective, and relative risk can be used.
The question is about not taking folate, so the No folate row is the exposed row. Having an NTD is the event column.
About 5.1 percent of infants had an NTD when the mother took no folate, against about 0.84 percent when she did.
The no folate risk is about six times the folate risk.
The risk that an infant develops one or more NTDs is about 6.1 times greater when the mother did not take folate than when she did.

examples.title: Odds ratio with a sentence
examples.prompt: Men with prostate cancer from a hospital database were cases, and matched men without prostate cancer were controls, in a retrospective case-control study. A \(\chi^2\) test found a difference (\(P<0.01\)). Quantify the association between smoking and prostate cancer in one sentence a newspaper reader could follow.

steps.say: The men were chosen because they did or did not have cancer, and then their smoking was looked up. So the study is retrospective and needs an odds ratio, not relative risk.
Smoking is the exposure and prostate cancer is the disease, so each count gets its exposure letter and its disease letter.
Multiply the smokers with cancer by the non smokers without cancer, then divide by the other cross product.
The odds of getting prostate cancer are about 1.5 times greater for men who smoke than for men who do not smoke.

examples.title: Number needed to treat
examples.prompt: People on dialysis were given placebo or aspirin. In the placebo group 18 of 25 developed thrombi, and in the aspirin group 6 of 19 did. How many people must be treated with aspirin for one more person to avoid a thrombus?

steps.say: Divide each group's thrombus count by its group size. About 72 percent of the placebo group and 32 percent of the aspirin group developed thrombi.
Aspirin lowers the thrombus rate by about 40 percentage points.
One over 0.4042 is 2.474, or about 2.5 people. A part of a person cannot be treated, so rounding up gives 3.

examples.title: Number needed to harm
examples.prompt: In a trial, 8 of 100 patients on a drug and 3 of 100 patients on placebo had a serious side effect. How many patients must take the drug for one extra patient to be harmed?

steps.say: Divide each side effect count by the group size, so the drug group rate is 8 percent and the placebo rate is 3 percent.
The drug raises the side effect rate by 5 percentage points.
One over 0.05 is exactly 20, so no rounding is needed. For every 20 patients who take the drug, one extra patient has the side effect.
